security_spec.violation_condition: XiangShan's instruction decoder funt5 comparator for the AMO opcode space fails to reject RESERVED encodings of Zalasr: (a) load-acquire with aq=0 (funct5=00110, aq=0) yields an undefined instruction that is decoded and executed rather than raising an illegal-instruction exception; (b) store-release with rl=0 (funct5=00111, rl=0) is similarly executed; (c) on RV64-only XiangShan configurations, ld.{aq,aqrl} or sd.{rl,aqrl} may be decoded and partially executed on a 32-bit datapath. Additionally, in the out-of-order LSU (Load-Store Unit), the acquire-RCsc ordering annotation (aq bit) is not propagated to the load-store queue, so younger loads/stores are permitted to commit before the acquire-load completes, violating the unidirectional fence semantics required by RISC-V RVWMO and creating architecturally observable reordering.
security_spec.summary: Zalasr introduces load-acquire (funct5=00110, mandatory aq=1) and store-release (funct5=00111, mandatory rl=1) under the AMO opcode; RESERVED encodings (aq=0 or rl=0) must trap via illegal-instruction exception, and RV64-only variants (ld/sd) must be rejected on RV32; hardware decoder rejection of reserved encodings and OoO LSU enforcement of acquire-release RCsc ordering are both security-critical implementation requirements
